avis.titre: On My Third Bottle - Great For Mature SkinOn My Third Bottle - Great For Mature Skin
avis.texte: At 52 with post-menopausal dry, mature skin, I’m constantly looking for products that support skin quality, elasticity, and long-term aging rather than just quick, temporary fixes. The numbuzin No.9 NAD+ Peptide Lifting Serum has become one of those rare products that I continue to repurchase — I’m currently on my third bottle, which says a lot. I’ve been especially interested in NAD+ as a topical ingredient, which has been gaining attention for its potential role in supporting skin energy, resilience, and overall skin health. While topical NAD+ isn’t going to create dramatic overnight changes, what it can do — and what this serum does very well — is improve overall skin quality, hydration, and firmness over time. The texture is excellent. It’s lightweight but slightly cushiony, almost like a silky essence-serum hybrid. It spreads easily, absorbs quickly, and layers beautifully with other products. Despite being lightweight, it still provides noticeable hydration, which is especially important for my dry, mature skin. What I’ve noticed most with consistent use is that my skin looks smoother, more refined, and more resilient. It’s not an instant dramatic change, but rather a gradual improvement in overall skin tone, bounce, and elasticity. These are exactly the types of results I look for at this stage — subtle but meaningful improvements over time. The formula also includes 50 peptides, which complement the NAD+ beautifully. Together, they create a serum focused on long-term

I've been very satisfied with this NAD+Peptide Lifting Serum. It is fragrance free and glides on like silk. The formula is in a pump bottle making application a breeze. Works well under a moisturizer, but you may find this cream provides enough hydration, as do I. (I am 63 years old). Most impressive was the soothing effect post 70% glycolic peel. I applied pure organic aloe vera gel immediately post peel. However, this cream provided more soothing from the sunburn feeling. Additionally, the peptide benefits are a win for me. Having said this, I am not a doctor or esthetician. I did my peel at home and chose the post treatment care without guidance. Medical advice is recommended. It’s just not in my budget to visit the dermatologist for skin care procedures. According to my own independent research, the ingredients in this cream are a good choice. Since a chemical peel is off topic, I will say that prior to my peel, the cream made my skin feel very soft to the touch and left a subtle glow. I haven't been using it long enough to notice any wrinkle reduction or skin plumping. Topicals take time.

Wow. Honestly, wow. This skincare product has been nothing but great and I mean it. The 50 Peptide + NDA formula is extremely potent and offers quick results a cheap price point. To go into more detail, it offers various branches of peptides, some that occur naturally in the body , like signaling peptides (which over time stimulate collagen) , so this product quite literally develops collagen , reinforcing it with NDA+. Along with those, it offers hydrating peptides with work at a molecular level to hydrate the skin. I had a bad breakout a week ago, and have been suffering with dry skin due to issues on dealing with the breakout, and this serum quite literally fixed it overnight. All I did was apply this along with other serums, and by morning time I noticed a reduction in redness, plumpiness of the skin which ultimately helped reduce fine lines, and hydration. This product is great for anyone with sensitive skin, heck if it can help someone with a breakout, what cant it do?! With that said, its also great if your skin is sensitive to fragrances, as it offers ZERO fragrance, all natural ingredients, and last you enough for about a month and a half. If your contemplating on buying this product, its a no brainer, GET IT. The presentation and packaging , along with the actual ease of incorporating to your skincare routine, and the BENEFITS will wow you.

avis.titre: NAD+ formula, without the luxury price tag.NAD+ formula, without the luxury price tag.
avis.texte: NAD+ supplements have steadily grown in popularity over the past decade, now skincare companies are trying to harness NAD+ anti-aging properties, focusing on skin longevity and slow aging. The science behind topical NAD+ is extremely new, and while promising; not very persuasive. Most topical NAD+ studies are non-peer reviewed, small sample sizes, and funded by the same company that makes said product. BUT… big names like Lancôme, Dermalogica, and Aramore have all recently released their own topical NAD+ formulas (with extremely high price tags to match) so there must be some promising research. I highly doubt those big names would wasting time, money, and their reputations on R&D and products that were entirely useless! Numbuzin’s No.9 NAD+ Peptide serum appears to use the same technology to incorporate NAD+ into a topical formulation as the big name companies, but at a much lower price. The additional 50 peptides is a huge plus- but there’s no ingredient list (at least not in English) indicating which ones are used, or their percentages. No.9 doesn’t feel like your typical serum. The consistency is super thick (it reminds me of Elmer’s glue!) and I need to use at least 3-4 pumps of product to cover my face. You can’t just pat this on like most serums; it needs to be applied like a cream or sunscreen, by gently rubbing it in. Despite looking sticky, it absorbs beautifully, and my dry skin just drinks it up. There’s definitely some nice hydration and slight plumping going on,
